SAR FloodWatch – Satellite-Based Flood Detection and Monitoring System

SAR FloodWatch is an interactive, satellite-based flood detection and monitoring platform developed by Team Pakoray in Space for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the Dancing with the SARs challenge.

Flood monitoring becomes particularly difficult during heavy rainfall and cloud cover, when traditional optical satellite imagery is often unavailable. Our solution uses Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery, which enables Earth observation regardless of cloud cover or daylight conditions.

Built using Python, Streamlit, and geospatial processing tools, SAR FloodWatch analyzes before-and-after Sentinel-1 satellite imagery using radar backscatter change detection to identify potential flooded areas. The platform generates flood segmentation masks, calculates estimated flooded areas, and visualizes results through interactive maps, image comparison sliders, and analytics dashboards.

Focusing initially on flood-prone regions of Pakistan, particularly Sindh, our project makes complex satellite observations more accessible and understandable.

By supporting faster visualization and assessment of potential flooding, SAR FloodWatch aims to assist researchers, disaster management authorities, and communities. Future development will integrate NASA-ISRO NISAR observations and advanced AI-based segmentation models.
details:
Project Details – NISAR FloodWatch

SAR FloodWatch is an interactive, satellite-based flood detection and monitoring platform developed by Team Pakoray in Space for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the Dancing with the SARs challenge. Our project aims to make satellite-based flood monitoring more accessible, understandable, and useful for disaster preparedness and response.

How Our Project Works

Floods often occur during periods of intense rainfall and heavy cloud cover, making traditional optical satellite imagery less effective. SAR FloodWatch addresses this challenge by using Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) technology, which can observe Earth's surface through clouds and during both day and night.

Our platform analyzes before-and-after SAR satellite images to identify potential flooded areas. Using a rule-based radar backscatter change detection algorithm, the system processes satellite observations and generates flood segmentation masks highlighting areas where flooding may have occurred.

Users can interact with the results through:

  • Interactive Flood Maps: Visualize detected flood areas geographically.
  • Before-and-After Comparison: Compare satellite observations using an interactive image slider.
  • Flood Detection: Generate flood masks and calculate estimated flooded areas in square kilometers.
  • Analytics Dashboard: Explore flood measurements, analysis history, and land-cover information from imported datasets.
  • Data Export: Download analysis results for further research and interpretation.

Technologies and Tools Used

We developed SAR FloodWatch using Python and Streamlit to create an accessible web application with an interactive interface.

Our main technologies include:

  • Python: Backend development and flood detection algorithms.
  • Streamlit: Web application development and user interface.
  • Rasterio and NumPy: Satellite raster processing and geospatial calculations.
  • SciPy and Scikit-image: Image processing and flood segmentation.
  • Folium: Interactive geographical maps and flood visualization.
  • Plotly and Pandas: Statistical analysis and interactive data visualization.
  • Sentinel-1 SAR Imagery: Satellite observations used for our initial flood detection workflow.
  • GitHub: Source code management and team collaboration.

Creativity and Innovation

What makes SAR FloodWatch innovative is its combination of satellite radar technology, automated image analysis, interactive visualization, and accessible flood information within a single platform.

Instead of requiring users to interpret complex satellite imagery manually, our application transforms radar observations into understandable flood maps, visual comparisons, and statistical summaries.

We initially focused on Sindh, Pakistan, a region vulnerable to severe flooding, while designing the platform to support analysis of other geographical areas.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Our project aims to support researchers, disaster management organizations, environmental monitoring teams, and communities by making flood-related satellite information easier to access and interpret.

Potential benefits include improved flood extent visualization, faster preliminary flood assessments, better understanding of affected geographical areas, and support for evidence-based disaster response planning.

During development, our team considered data accessibility, satellite image alignment, geospatial accuracy, ease of use, and the importance of distinguishing possible flood detections from confirmed flooding.

Future Development: We aim to integrate NASA-ISRO NISAR satellite observations, incorporate validated deep learning models such as U-Net, and expand the platform's capabilities for monitoring flood-prone regions worldwide.

Ultimately, SAR FloodWatch demonstrates how space technology and accessible software can help turn complex Earth observation data into meaningful information for disaster resilience and environmental monitoring.
